eligibility.text: Every applicant must appear in person to register, at a designated NIA registration office or a Ghana Mission. Nobody can register on your behalf, and you cannot register on anyone else's.
All Ghanaian citizens aged zero and above living in Ghana.
All Ghanaian citizens aged zero and above living outside Ghana.
Children under six are linked to a parent's Ghana Card, and their own biometrics are captured when they turn six.

Applicants who cannot travel to a centre - including people who are hospitalised, imprisoned or physically challenged - are served by mobile units or assisted at the centre by a relative or friend. Being assisted is not the same as being represented: the applicant is still present.
All foreign nationals legally and permanently resident in Ghana, handled under a separate scheme with its own fees.

documents.note: Either one relative aged 18 or over who has already registered, or two people aged 18 or over holding Ghana Cards from listed professions - teachers, chiefs, magistrates, licensed professionals, civil servants, clergy, security personnel, or current and past elected officials.

steps.action: Your personal information is captured into the National Identity Register
Your biometrics are captured - fingerprints, irises, photograph and signature
You review and confirm the information recorded

Book a registration appointment and pay the fee for your region at the time of booking
Attend the appointment in person at the designated registration centre or Ghana Mission - attendance in person is required and cannot be delegated
Your completed application form is reviewed and your personal information captured into the National Identity Register
Your biometrics are captured - ten fingerprints, irises, photograph and signature
You review and sign or thumbprint the printout of your captured information, correcting anything wrong before it is accepted
Your Ghana Card is printed and issued to you using your biometrics

First-time registration, 25 years and above, at a district office

timeline.note: NIA does not publish a processing or issuance time. Premium centres are presented as same-visit issuance but no official turnaround figure exists.

rejection_causes.text: Not having any of the four accepted citizenship documents, and no eligible voucher.
Vouchers who do not meet the age or profession criteria.
No digital address code for your residence.

caveats.text: NIA fees changed on 2 February 2026 under L.I. 2512. Any guide published before that date quotes superseded amounts.

NIA's own pages disagree about diaspora registration: the service page publishes fees and a procedure, while an older FAQ says registration abroad will open 'at a later date'. Confirm with the Ghana Mission nearest the applicant before anyone pays or travels.

eligibility.text: Ghanaian citizens by birth, naturalisation or registration.
Applicants under 18 need parental or legal-guardian consent on the form.

documents.name: Completed passport application form
Evidence of citizenship and identity - birth certificate, Ghana Card, old passport, voter ID, or a dual citizenship, naturalisation or registration certificate
Two guarantors who are living relatives
documents.note: The form states guarantors agree jointly and severally to pay any expenses the government incurs if you are repatriated or die abroad. This is why the relationship requirement is strict.

documents.name: Endorsement by an eligible witness
documents.where_to_obtain: A person in a listed profession
documents.note: The form lists clergy, military officers, civil servants, medical practitioners, legal professionals, educators and registered professionals.

documents.name: Proof of profession
documents.note: Employed applicants need an employer letter or work ID; students a student ID; self-employed a business registration certificate. Unemployed and informal-sector applicants do not need this.

documents.name: Parental consent
documents.note: Required for applicants under 18.

documents.name: Proof of name change by affidavit or Gazette publication
documents.where_to_obtain: Commissioner for Oaths or Ghana Publishing Company
documents.note: Required only if your name has changed.

steps.action: Create an account and complete the application online
Pay the fee - Ecobank, GCB, Zenith Bank or the Ghana.Gov platform, by card or mobile money
Print the completed form, have it endorsed by an eligible witness and complete the guarantor sections
Submit it in person at a passport application centre - the form requires personal submission
Have your biometrics captured at the centre
Track the status through the e-tracking system
Receive the passport by courier nationwide, or collect it
steps.note: The Ministry states the courier fee is already included in the GH¢350 standard fee.

fees.label: Standard application, 32-page ordinary booklet
fees.note: The Ministry announced this reduced fee effective 13 November 2025. The official application portal was still displaying GH¢500 when we last checked. Both are official sources and they disagree - confirm at the point of payment.

fees.label: Fees still shown on the application portal
fees.amount_text: 32-page standard GH¢500, 48-page standard GH¢644, 32-page expedited GH¢700, 48-page expedited GH¢800
fees.note: These are the pre-November-2025 amounts. Shown here because the official portal still displays them.

fees.label: Current 48-page booklet fee
fees.note: No official source published a 48-page figure after the November 2025 reduction.

timeline.expedited: A 24-hour service exists at GH¢2,000. Earlier announcements mentioned 5 working days and 3 days - these figures have not been reconciled publicly
timeline.note: The standard 15 working days is consistent across Ministry statements. The expedited tiers are not.

rejection_causes.text: The guarantor section is incomplete, or the guarantors are not living relatives as the form requires.
The form has not been endorsed by a witness in one of the listed professional categories.
The application was not submitted in person by the applicant.
A name change is not evidenced by an affidavit or Gazette publication.

Guides widely claim that a name mismatch against your Ghana Card causes rejection. We could not find any official source stating this rule, so it is repeated here only as an unverified claim - though matching your names is sensible anyway.

caveats.text: Two official sources disagree about the standard fee. The Ministry announced GH¢350 from 13 November 2025; the application portal still showed GH¢500. Take money for the higher figure or confirm before you travel.
The live official portal is passport.mfa.gov.gh. The domain passport.gov.gh does not resolve - any site using that name is not the official Passport Office portal.
Rejection-rate percentages circulate widely online for Ghanaian passport applications. None is traceable to an official publication, so we do not repeat any figure.

eligibility.text: You must already hold a Ghanaian passport.

Your old Ghana passport

Pay the fee
Print and endorse the form

Have your biometrics captured
Track the status, then collect or receive the passport by courier

fees.label: Renewal fee
fees.note: No official source publishes a renewal fee separate from the first-application fee. The standard 32-page fee of GH¢350 from 13 November 2025 is the best available figure, and the application portal still shows GH¢500. Confirm at the point of payment.

timeline.standard: 15 working days, the same as a first application
timeline.expedited: The 24-hour service at GH¢2,000 is available
timeline.note: The one renewal-specific timing rule is that you may apply from six months before expiry.

rejection_causes.text: Applying earlier than six months before expiry.
Submitting photocopies where originals are required.
No police report and affidavit where the old passport is lost.

caveats.text: The clearest official renewal document lists come from Ghana's missions abroad in Berlin and Hamburg. We could not find an equivalent page published for applications made inside Ghana, so requirements at a domestic centre may differ. Confirm before you travel to a centre.

eligibility.text: You must be 18 years or above to qualify to apply for a driver's licence.

Every licence holder is required by law to take an eye test. Since 1 July 2022 it is done at a designated optical centre by a registered optometrist or ophthalmologist, not at a DVLA office, under Regulation 29 of L.I. 2180.
A Ghana Card is used for identity verification.
First-time applicants must complete training at a DVLA-certified driving school - reported as a 48-hour course, with no exemption for experienced drivers.

Sit the computer-based theory test
steps.note: The pass mark is reported as 70%. DVLA has said tests are offered in local languages.

steps.action: Take the practical driving test with a DVLA examiner
Collect the licence card at the DVLA office, or receive it by courier

fees.label: Driving school course fee

fees.label: Eye test fee

timeline.standard: Reported as 2 to 4 weeks for the biometric smart card
timeline.expedited: Prestige and Ultra centres offer faster service, but DVLA publishes no service level
timeline.note: DVLA publishes no official turnaround time.

rejection_causes.text: Failing the computer-based theory test or the practical driving test.
Failing the mandatory eye test.

eligibility.text: Every person resident in Ghana other than the Armed Forces and the Ghana Police Service must belong to a health insurance scheme licensed under the Act.

Exempt groups who do not pay the processing fee: pregnant women, indigents, categories of differently-abled persons determined by the Minister, persons with mental disorder, SSNIT contributors, SSNIT pensioners, persons above seventy years of age, and other categories prescribed by the Minister.
There is no age floor - newborn babies can be registered.
A Ghana Card is required to register on the MyNHIS app.

documents.name: Ghana Card
documents.note: Mandatory for registering through the MyNHIS app.

documents.name: Personal details - name, date of birth, age, marital status, phone number and residential address
documents.where_to_obtain: You provide this at the interview

documents.name: Photograph and biometrics - fingerprints from all ten fingers
Proof of pregnancy for the pregnancy exemption - a current antenatal card, a doctor or midwife note, an endorsed pregnancy test, or an ultrasound report
SSNIT number or active contributor status, for the SSNIT exemption
Your old NHIS card or membership number
documents.note: Needed for renewal.

steps.action: Attend an interview at an NHIS district office to determine whether you are a premium-paying or exempt member
Provide your personal information
Have your photograph and fingerprints from all ten fingers captured
Select your preferred primary care provider - a clinic, health centre, polyclinic or primary hospital
Pay the premium and processing fee unless you are in an exempt group, and receive your membership
Renew every year - at a district office, by dialling *929# on any network, or through the MyNHIS app
steps.note: Pregnant women and indigents should renew or register in person so the exemption is applied correctly rather than being charged through the app.

fees.label: Premium and processing fee
fees.note: The NHIA publishes no amount anywhere on its website. Premiums are set at district level and are not uniform nationally. Ask at your district office.

fees.label: Processing fee for exempt groups
fees.note: Pregnant women, indigents, SSNIT contributors and pensioners, people over seventy and the other listed categories do not pay the processing fee.

timeline.standard: Membership lasts one year and must be renewed annually. A one-month waiting period normally applies before benefits start
timeline.note: Renewal by *929# is effectively instant. NHIA publishes no card issuance turnaround.

rejection_causes.text: Registering through the MyNHIS app when you are in an exempt group, which can result in being charged incorrectly. Register in person instead.

caveats.text: The NHIA waived registration fees, renewal fees and the one-month waiting period nationwide from 6 to 31 May 2026 under Operation STORM. Standard fees and the waiting period resumed on 1 June 2026. Coverage from May 2026 saying NHIS is free is now out of date.
The NHIA does not publish contact details or fee amounts in a form we could retrieve. Both need confirming at a district office.
